issues.description: use_koji_url_only has no stated precondition; nevra[0] silently crashes or misroutes when nevra is empty or starts with a non-letter
issues.detail: The author has not stated the precondition on url_list. The construction nevra = url.split('/')[-1] followed by nevra[0].lower() presumes a non-empty trailing path component beginning with a lowercase-mappable letter. A URL ending in '/' yields an empty string and an IndexError; a NEVRA whose first character is a digit (rare for Fedora, but the function has no business assuming it) silently produces a wrong koji path under '/0/' or '/1/'. Either the precondition is 'url ends in a non-empty package filename whose first character is a letter' and it must be asserted, or the function must reject malformed inputs. Neither is done.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returning None is not handled; the caller will happily synthesize a URL containing the literal string 'None'
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url is documented to extract the arch, but its postcondition is in fact 'returns one of the four arches, or None'. The caller use_koji_url_only does not test for None; it concatenates the result into an f-string, producing '/latest/None/Packages/...'. This is precisely the class of defect that arises when a function's postcondition is left implicit. Either the function must guarantee a valid arch (and raise otherwise), or the caller must handle None explicitly. The present code does neither, which is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE in reverse: no defense at all where the type system gave a clear warning.

issues.description: No invariant or termination argument for the silent first-match heuristic in extract_arch_from_url
issues.detail: The regex picks the first occurrence of any known arch substring anywhere in the URL. The invariant the author appears to want is 'the matched arch is the package arch'. That invariant is not stated, and it is not in general true: a mirror path, a username, a project name, or a future repository layout could contain 'x86_64' before the package's true arch segment. The word-boundary comment defends against substring matches but not against legitimate-but-wrong earlier occurrences. The correct discipline is to derive the arch from a known position in the URL or from the NEVRA itself (the '.arch.rpm' suffix), not to scan and pray.

issues.description: Race condition acknowledged in the commit message is left entirely unguarded in the code
issues.detail: The author concedes 'a possible race condition between the koji tag operation and the CI/CD system building hermetically' and proceeds to ship anyway. This is TESTED-NOT-PROVED at the system level: the correctness of the produced lockfile depends on a remote, asynchronous tagging operation that the code neither waits for nor verifies. At minimum there should be a verification step that HEAD-checks the synthesized URLs, or a documented retry/wait protocol. 'It's ok because it's Konflux only' is a scope argument, not a correctness argument.

issues.description: The arch list is duplicated knowledge
issues.detail: The set {x86_64, aarch64, ppc64le, s390x} is hard-coded inside extract_arch_from_url with no link to wherever the rest of the program enumerates supported arches. When a new arch is added, this function will silently return None for it and the caller will silently produce '/None/' URLs. The single source of truth for supported arches should be named once and referenced; here it is copied.

issues.description: The existing prioritization loop in query_packages_location is now dead reasoning
issues.detail: With use_koji_url_only running on every result, the upstream 'prioritize coreos-pool' logic in query_packages_location is redundant: every non-pool URL will be rewritten downstream. Leaving both in place means the program now expresses two overlapping policies for the same property, and a future reader must reason about their interaction. Either remove the upstream prioritization or document precisely why both layers exist.

review.summary: The patch substitutes one heuristic (prefer coreos-pool URL when present) for another (rewrite every non-pool URL into a synthesized coreos-pool path). Neither function carries a stated precondition, postcondition, or invariant; both contain failure modes the author has not reasoned about: empty NEVRA splits, first-character indexing, unhandled None returns, and first-match arch scanning that can pick the wrong substring in a structurally different URL. The acknowledged race against the koji tagger is shipped without guard or verification on the synthesized URLs. The change is TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best and UNREASONED at the function level; I would refuse it in this form and require explicit specifications, a verified arch source (the .arch.rpm suffix of the NEVRA, not a scan of the URL), and either a wait/verify step against coreos-pool or an honest comment that the lockfile may reference not-yet-tagged artifacts.
